explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is about the library's own map `bcHom` (defined at line 19 of the same file) between the coordinate rings of the base-changed curves `W⁄K` and `W⁄K'`. Mathlib does have the related map `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.CoordinateRing.map` (Affine/Point.lean, line 184), but in the Mathlib sources I found no lemma about how `XYIdeal` behaves under any ring map. Grepping for `XYIdeal` together with `map` turned up only uses inside the proofs of `quotientXYIdealEquiv` and `XYIdeal_add_eq`. The base-change lemmas in Affine/Basic.lean and Affine/Formula.lean only cover the polynomial, equation, nonsingularity and the addition formulas, not ideals of the coordinate ring. The library's proof uses only generic Mathlib lemmas (`Ideal.map_span`, `Set.image_pair`, `Polynomial.map_sub`, `Polynomial.map_C`, `Polynomial.map_X`) together with its own `bcHom_mk`.
